newsitem.title: DENMARK: SAS slams new air travel passenger taxes.
newsitem.headline: SAS slams new air travel passenger taxes.

text.p: Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS) said on Monday that new government passenger taxes on air travel would cut into earnings on low price air tickets to such an extent that it might be forced to to cease cheap air fare offers.

"The proposed passenger tax would entirely erode earnings from the sale of low price air tickets and might possibly force SAS to do away with cheap air travel offers," SAS information chief Troels Rasmussen told Reuters.
He said he estimated that the proposed new taxes could double the price of some budget air tickets.

Earlier the Danish centre-left minority government said it agreed with far-left parliamentary parties on a two billion crown package of economic measures including new passenger taxes on domestic air travel and increased taxes on overseas air travel.

According to a Finance Ministry statement, the package would impose a new, unspecified passenger tax on domestic flights while at the same time increasing passenger taxes on foreign travel to 75 crowns per head from the present 65 crowns. --Per Bech Thomsen, Copenhagen newsroom +45-33969656
